title: Oven-Roasted Delightful Chinese Pork Mu-Shu
description: A Hunan-style Chinese dish featuring crispy pork, crunchy vegetables, and a tangy sauce, all wrapped up in a crispy mu-shu pancake. This recipe is inspired by the flavors of Hunan Province, China.

ingredients.name: mu-shu pancake
ingredients.notes: available at most Asian markets or online

instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together soy sauce, vinegar, hoisin sauce, and cornstarch. Add the pork and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Remove the pork from the marinade and place it on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Roast in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, or until cooked through.
While the pork is roasting, heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the scallions and cook until crispy, about 3-4 minutes. Set aside.
In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil. Add the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the cooked pork to the skillet and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the soy sauce mixture to the skillet and stir to combine. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.

To assemble the mu-shu, place a few slices of the pork mixture onto a mu-shu pancake, followed by a few slices of scallion, a sprinkle of green onions, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Roll up the pancake tightly and serve immediately.
Repeat with the remaining pork mixture and pancakes.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the hoisin sauce and bring to a simmer. Cook until thickened, about 5 minutes. Set aside to cool.
Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Discard the solids and stir in the soy sauce and vinegar. Set aside to cool.

To make the mu-shu pancakes, combine the flour, cornstarch, and salt in a large bowl. Gradually add the warm water, stirring with a fork until the dough comes together. Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic. Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball. Flatten each ball into a disk and wrap in plastic wrap. Let rest for 30 minutes before rolling out to a thin circle. Cook in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes on each side, until crispy and golden. Repeat with the remaining dough.

To assemble the mu-shu, place a few slices of the pork mixture onto a mu-shu pancake, followed by a few slices of scallion, a sprinkle of green onions, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Roll up the pancake tightly and serve immediately.
Repeat with the remaining pork mixture and pancakes.
